group.passage:
Meningitis is a disease that involves membranes, or thin coverings, around the brain and spinal cord. Normally, a shield called the blood-brain barrier (BBB) keeps bacteria, viruses, and fungi out, but sometimes they manage to break through. [[1]] That would trigger people’s immune system. When the immune system responds, the meninges, or the membranes that encase the brain and the spinal cord, become inflamed. Meningitis has three classic symptoms: a high fever, a bad headache, and a stiff neck. People with meningitis may also be tired and have a rash.
Bacterial and viral meningitis are the most common types. Meningitis caused by bacteria is usually more serious. [[2]] In some cases, deaths could be within a matter of hours. Viral meningitis, on the other hand, is usually less severe. However, it can be hard to tell at an early stage which kinds of meningitis a patient is infected with. [[3]] Looking into a person’s blood or withdrawing a sample of the fluid from around their spine can determine exactly either bacteria or viruses are causing the meningitis. But it takes time to get these kinds of test results. If there is any chance that bacteria might be responsible, doctors have to respond immediately, delivering antibiotics directly into a person’s blood via a vein.
The good news is that meningitis can be prevented. The best way to protect against the disease is vaccination. Researchers have developed a range of vaccines directed against as many bacteria and viruses as possible. [[4]] While meningitis is much less common now than in the past, being familiar with the symptoms is always a good idea to keep ourselves away from the disease.

options_bank.A: It can lead to brain damage, paralysis, hearing loss, or learning disabilities.
options_bank.B: Besides, maintaining healthy habits, practicing good hygiene, and not having close contact with people who are sick can also help.
options_bank.C: When this happens, an infection can start to grow in the fluid that surrounds the brain.
options_bank.D: For this reason, suspected cases of meningitis are always medical emergencies.
